subject_area: Relational database fundamentals — design, SQL, internals
pedagogical_level: undergraduate fundamentals course with hands-on SQL practice
course_intent: Teach the foundational theory and practice of relational databases — students should leave able to model data with ER/EER diagrams, map conceptual designs to relational schemas, write and reason about SQL queries, normalize schemas, and understand the basics of file organization and indexing that underlie a single-node DBMS.
depth_bound: Recommendations stay at the relational-fundamentals + hands-on-SQL level, including conceptual coverage of single-node storage and indexing. Distributed databases, NoSQL engines, query optimizer internals, transaction/concurrency-control algorithms beyond ACID basics, and DBMS implementation internals are beyond this course's depth.
key_topics: ER and EER modeling (entities, relationships, weak entities, specialization/generalization)
Relational algebra (SELECT, PROJECT, JOIN variants, DIVISION)
SQL DDL and DML with hands-on queries (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)
Complex SQL (nested queries, EXISTS, joins, GROUP BY/HAVING, aggregates)
Views and SQL authorization (GRANT/REVOKE, view-based access control)
File organization (heap, sorted, static and extendible/dynamic hashing)
Single-level and multilevel indexing (primary, clustering, secondary, B+-tree concepts)
one_liner: Single-node relational database fundamentals covering ER/EER design, schema mapping, relational algebra, SQL (basic and complex), normalization, and conceptual coverage of file organization and indexing — distributed databases, NoSQL, transaction/concurrency internals, and query optimizer engineering are out of scope.
